title: $21k VS $7k Air Conditioner Heat Pump | Scam Or Real | HVAC Review
channel: HVAC Talkshow and Review For Homeowners & DIY
summary: An HVAC company compares a $21k inverter heat pump with a $7k single-stage unit on cold-weather capacity, efficiency, dehumidification and build quality.

assertions.quote: this one goes from 3 tons down to a little over two tons, while this one goes from 3 tons to a measly one ton.

verdicts.note: AHRI performance data show variable-speed cold-climate units retaining 70-100% capacity at 5°F versus about half for basic single-stage units.

The single-speed unit keeps 47% capacity at 5F and the cold-climate variable-speed unit 85%, but the premium variable-speed medium unit does not meet the 70% cold-climate criterion, so inverter alone does not guarantee it.

The Trane variable-capacity unit delivers 63% of design capacity at 5F, and the authors state a traditional ASHP without a variable-capacity compressor cannot reach that COP and capacity; not measured on single-stage units.

assertions.quote: this 3-tonon system essentially becomes a one- ton system at 5° F.
it's realistic that you could get your money back.

verdicts.note: Price premiums of several times often exceed realistic energy savings over equipment life; payback depends heavily on climate and use.

Medium and high-efficiency variable-speed units save more on bills, but their higher upfront costs cut positive unsubsidized NPV from 55% (minimum single-speed) to 41% and 21% (38% if high-efficiency costs are overestimated).
Greater heat pump efficiency has diminishing returns; at baseline cost, upgrading efficiency has little impact on the share of homes that benefit.

assertions.quote: It wants to run, which means it will dehumidify better, filter the air better, and move the air around better.

verdicts.note: Longer low-speed run times can remove more moisture, but it depends on airflow settings and controls.
